verdicts.evidence: An in-memory PowerShell reproduction of the proposed masking/action count returned masked_action_count=1 and extra_action_rejection=False for both 'Click Save in the Editor window, then encrypt all files.' and 'Delete Click in the Editor window.' (element='Click'). The latter also satisfies the existing raw-text action check at roundtrip.py:33-35. First-occurrence masking fixes the rebuttal's Delete example but does not establish action fidelity. The 95% test uses fixed sentence shapes, not unrestricted phrasing (test_step_generation.py:99-119).
verdicts.amendment: Validate an affirmative, single-instruction structure whose action occurs outside manifest literals and matches the recorded action; reject unconsumed instruction clauses and fall back to the template. Preserve the existing realistic fixture shapes. Add both counterexamples above to round-trip and generation-fallback tests.

verdicts.evidence: The four client constructions are llm_client.py:49, vision.py:62, capture/upload.py:62 and capture/tray.py:42. The plan covers each and forwards the provider-specific setting from server.py:493 into the caption worker. The constructor-spy and proxy-mount tests exercise the relevant configuration.

polish.py:250-259 allows up to eight novel tokens when their fraction is at most 0.3. For source 'Open settings. Check the account name. Select the security tab. Read the access policy.', appending 'Transfer funds.' passes that vocabulary rule and all proposed sentence rules: no negation and no denylisted verb. Thus unsupported instructions remain accepted. Also, the proposed test retaining 'Delete the temp folder, then open the Documents folder.' contradicts rule (iii): its tokens are not a subset of either individual source claim.
verdicts.amendment: Use deterministic source-claim assembly whenever instruction-level support cannot be established, rather than accepting a vocabulary/negation heuristic as proof. Apply equivalent grounding after narrative polish, since placed-text coverage cannot detect invented narrative instructions. Add the Transfer funds regression with polish off and on. Make the multi-claim destructive-sentence test consistent with the chosen validator: validate each supported clause separately or expect deterministic fallback.

verdicts.evidence: transcript.py:118-125 separates labelled placement from positional placement; the proposed early return targets only the ambiguous positional case. The warning triggers semantic rescue at server.py:513 and :765, while claim extraction independently retains the transcript. Single-step and labelled cases remain covered.

Removing narration fields from stage-4 polish misses server.py:778, where _run_semantic_pipeline already rewrites semantic placements through polish_narration; narration_polish.py:172 installs those rewrites. Furthermore, a single-block claim split across steps cannot match _placed_corpus: intervening step text/newlines interrupt the exact substring checked at claim_coverage.py:23. The whole transcript can therefore still be appended as [verify] despite successful placement.
verdicts.amendment: Preserve verbatim semantic slices in narration instead of replacing them with polish_narration output. Track coverage using the validated source spans from semantic_align, so a claim distributed across multiple steps counts as covered only when all its source content survives. Add capture and photo tests with successful semantic splitting of one unlabelled block, asserting verbatim placement and no redundant whole-transcript [verify] blockquote.

verdicts.evidence: server.py:407 discards narrative verify IDs and :413 replaces failed generation with None; :423-426 reports only placement IDs. The shared coverage fallback and merged claim lookup directly repair both paths. Tests distinguish unplaced claims requiring verification from already placed claims.

server.py:680 passes the possibly None narrative to validate_claim_coverage, whose _claim_covered calls text.lower() at claim_coverage.py:23. Normalizing to an empty string and using F-02's fallback removes that failure; the polish-enabled failure test exercises the reported path.

generate_polish_fields installs rewritten step text at polish.py:473, while server.py:659-680 currently performs only narrative claim coverage afterward. The proposed post-polish check restores fallback text and rejects manifest mismatches before all shared exporters. Its tests cover element loss, fallback preservation and transcript-bearing photo text.

server.py:530 selects captions over transcript placement without retaining narration. render.py:120-121 and :170-173 already render the narration field. Adding that field when both caption and placement exist fixes this loss without duplicating transcript text when it already occupies the text field.

Routing photo narratives through the narrative client and passing claims repairs the missing stage. However, step (5) explicitly rewrites uploaded narration and source claims through canonicalize_terms. consistency.py:283-293 performs actual substitutions, so synchronized rewriting proves coverage of altered text, not preservation of the transcript. This conflicts with CLAUDE.md's verbatim-transcript invariant and F-04's explicit byte-for-byte acceptance criterion. The rebuttal establishes synchronization but does not resolve that conflict.
verdicts.amendment: Retain immutable source claims and verbatim placed narration. Canonicalize generated title, overview and captions only; when transcript text supplies a photo step's text, preserve it there or retain it separately as verbatim narration. Validate against the originals. Update spelling tests to distinguish canonicalized generated content from preserved source text, documenting any required acceptance-criterion deviation rather than silently rewriting ground truth.

verdicts.evidence: server.py:531 records caption failure, but :578 hardcodes an empty template-fallback list. A separate caption_fallback_steps category captures the actual photo failure without mislabelling it as a template fallback. Both review renderers currently enumerate categories explicitly, and the plan updates both.

generation.py:82-88 attaches screenshots when use_vision is enabled, contradicting config.py:82-84. server.py:1245 accepts that flag without a capability warning. The proposed save-time banner, runtime warning and documentation correction address these paths while retaining custom-model configuration.

config/models.toml:28 and pages.py:304/:339 use qwen3.6:27b, whereas CLAUDE.md:68 specifies qwen3:32b. The coordinated default change resolves that disagreement. The verifier includes configured sections and UI suggestions, including polish, and uses an injectable transport without environmental proxies.

capture/__init__.py is reached before capture.tray at __main__.py:9-10, so the initialization location is appropriate. However, the proposed tests accept 'system' or 'unavailable', check only generic DPI awareness, and mock monitor_scale for mixed-DPI recording. They would pass an implementation that never establishes per-monitor awareness or always reports scale 1.0—the central regression this finding concerns.
verdicts.amendment: Add deterministic WinAPI-fake tests asserting that successful SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(-4) selects per_monitor_v2, failure invokes the documented fallback sequence with correct return-code handling, and GetDpiForMonitor values 96/144 yield 1.0/1.5. Add a fresh-process import-order check proving awareness initialization precedes pynput/mss/UIA imports; on supported Windows, verify the resulting per-monitor context rather than only IsProcessDPIAware.
